why_silent: mis-paired/NaN values are plausible numbers; code runs clean
why_nonobvious: not a statistic choice — pandas aligns by index/position, not by key
boundary: undetectable only if result drops the key AND the value multiset coincides
wrong_detail: by-key combine wrong at id(s) [1, 2, 3, 4] (positional mis-alignment / spurious NaN)
correct_detail: every id's combined value matches by-key recomputation

why_silent: 1001 is a valid-looking number; no error on astype(int)
why_nonobvious: a framework cast, not a math error; classic leading-zero ID loss
generic_catch: weak: a dtype-aware validity check could notice the type change
boundary: only matters for codes with leading zeros / >15-digit precision

why_nonobvious: groupby silently drops NaN KEYS by default (dropna=True)
boundary: no firing if the key column has no NaN
wrong_detail: total 70 < input 150: NaN-key rows silently dropped

why_silent: one row per id is returned; values are real rows
why_nonobvious: drop_duplicates keeps FIRST on UNSORTED data, not the intended latest/max
boundary: needs an explicit 'which row' intent (latest/max) to define correctness
wrong_detail: kept non-latest row for id(s) [1, 2] (drop_duplicates keep=first on unsorted)
correct_detail: kept the max-order row per key

why_silent: totals conserve; a normal hourly table is returned
why_nonobvious: default closed='left'/label='left' silently moves boundary points to the wrong bin
generic_catch: none (sum conservation holds for both — only per-bin differs)
boundary: requires intent to pin closed/label; pure conservation cannot distinguish
correct_detail: bin sums match intended closed/label convention

why_silent: a left join returns all rows; missing prices are just NaN
why_nonobvious: case/whitespace mismatch silently fails the match, not a logic error
generic_catch: none (NaN lookups look like genuine misses)
boundary: cannot tell intended-miss from normalization-miss without a normalization rule
wrong_detail: NaN lookup for key(s) ['Apple ', 'CHERRY'] that DO match after normalization

why_silent: a clean per-cat total; just numerically inflated
why_nonobvious: many-to-many join duplicates rows (SQL fan-out), the #1 silent SQL bug
boundary: only additive left-measures; counts/ratios need a different invariant
wrong_detail: measure total 1000 != pre-join 600: join fan-out duplicated rows

why_silent: smaller counts that look like real group sizes
why_nonobvious: COUNT(col) vs COUNT(*) NULL semantics (pandas .count skips NaN)
boundary: no firing if the counted column has no NULLs
wrong_detail: record count != group size for ['A', 'B']: COUNT(col) dropped NULL rows

why_silent: model trains/scores fine; ONLY the held-out score is silently optimistic
why_nonobvious: test stats leak into the scaler — invalidates the whole evaluation, not one cell
generic_catch: none (exec-pass + range both miss; this is the highest-impact case)
boundary: only OBSERVABLE when train/test distributions differ — but that is exactly when it biases results
wrong_detail: train slice mean=-0.998 != 0 (std=0.056): scaled with GLOBAL stats (test leaked into fit)
correct_detail: train slice mean=0.000 (~0), std=1.000: fit on train, no leakage

why_silent: downstream .mean() of the (n,n) array is a plausible scalar
why_nonobvious: silent broadcasting of (n,) vs (n,1), not an algorithm error
generic_catch: shape validity could catch it BEFORE it is aggregated to a scalar
boundary: once reduced to a scalar the shape evidence is gone; catch it at the array step
correct_detail: result is length-4 vector as intended

why_silent: points still plot; just in the wrong place
why_nonobvious: lat/lon order convention differs across libraries
generic_catch: YES: a generic [-90,90] range check also catches it (lower novelty)
boundary: undetectable when all true longitudes also fall within [-90,90]

why_silent: a normal-looking return column; backtests just look too good
why_nonobvious: uses FUTURE data (look-ahead bias) — silent and devastating in finance/forecasting
boundary: constant-growth series make past==future returns; needs varying returns to expose
